key_insight: A physics-informed neural network linking accretion-shock physics to planetary evolution predicts hotter, higher-entropy gas giants with intrinsic luminosities 4–10 times those of cold-start models.
engineering_relevance: The coupled workflow connects detailed shock simulations to long-term planetary evolution, improving model-based interpretation of directly imaged exoplanets.
method: Train a physics-informed neural network on 1,000 first-principles accretion-shock simulations.
Include radiation hydrodynamics and molecular hydrogen dissociation.
Use predicted post-shock boundary conditions in MESA planetary-evolution calculations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a sharp post-shock entropy jump near hydrogen dissociation at approximately 2,000 K and evolved intrinsic luminosities 4–10 times higher than cold-start predictions.
watch_item: Magnetic-field estimates are optimistic upper limits, and the abstract provides no held-out prediction errors or observational validation.
paper_title: Thermodynamics of gas giants accreting via shocks: the role of molecular hydrogen dissociation
